title: Attach/Detach failures + kubelet bootloop — incident breadcrumbs
content:
Summary:
One of our recent scale-up events produced a subset of nodes that never reached Ready. Symptoms looked like: kubelet repeatedly restarting (bootloop), pods stuck in ContainerCreating with PersistentVolume attach/detach errors. This doc is my scratchpad of commands run, outputs, hypotheses, and experiments.

Environment/context:
- Cluster: prod-us-west-2 (managed by our infra repo bootstrap scripts)
- K8s: 1.25.4 -> nodes use Ubuntu 22.04, containerd 1.6.18
- CNI: Calico v3.25 (Helm chart deployed via infra helm-operator)
- CSI driver: gce-pd-csi v1.6.0 (upgraded two weeks ago as part of node image rollout)
- Autoscaling: cluster-autoscaler triggered scale-up for spike in inference jobs

Initial symptom timeline (approx):
- 2024-02-14 02:11 UTC: cluster-autoscaler requested 4 new nodes (p-small-preemptible)
- 02:19 UTC: nodes boot & start joining; 3 become Ready, 1 stuck NotReady
- 02:27 UTC: multiple pods pending on the stuck node (PVC attach fails)
- 02:29 UTC: noticed kubelet on that node in restart loop (systemd restarts every ~40s)

Commands and outputs (copied directly):
1) Check node status from control-plane:
$ kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep ip-10-0-
ip-10-0-54-81   NotReady  8d  v1.25.4  10.0.54.81  us-west-2a  <none>  <none>

2) Describe node to see taints/conditions:
$ kubectl describe node ip-10-0-54-81
...
Conditions:
  Type             Status  LastHeartbeatTime                 Message
  ----             ------  -----------------                 -------
  Ready            False   2024-02-14T02:28:50Z            KubeletNotReady: kubelet is not ready: failed to start kubelet: device attach failed

3) Look at kubelet journal: (ssh to node)
$ sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager
Feb 14 02:27:41 ip-10-0-54-81 kubelet[1217]: E0214 02:27:41.234 1217 kubelet_volume_manager.go:281] attachdetach-controller failed to attach volume "pvc-0b9f..." on node "ip-10-0-54-81": rpc error: code = Unknown desc = attach failed: volume not attached
Feb 14 02:27:45 ip-10-0-54-81 kubelet[1217]: E0214 02:27:45.667 1217 kubelet.go:1854] Failed to start kubelet: failed to ensure kubelet is running: failed to reconcile node status: attach/detach controller has errors
Feb 14 02:27:45 ip-10-0-54-81 systemd[1]: kubelet.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE

4) Container runtime check:
$ sudo systemctl status containerd
Active: active (running) since Feb 14 02:20
$ sudo crictl ps -a
CONTAINER ID  IMAGE  CREATED  STATE  NAMES
(no  containers)

5) CSI driver logs on the node (gce-pd-csi):
$ sudo journalctl -u pd-csi-driver -n 200 --no-pager
Feb 14 02:26:59 pd-csi: I0214 02:26:59 controller.go:230] NodePublishVolume RPC failed for volume "vol-0b9f...": rpc error: code = Internal desc = failed to find device path for attached disk

6) dmesg / kernel-related hints:
$ sudo dmesg | tail -n 80
[  7042.123456] scsi 0:0:0:0: Direct-Access     Google  PersistentDisk     1.0
[  7042.123467] sd 0:0:0:0: Attached scsi generic sg0 type 0
[  7042.123789] sd 0:0:0:0: [sda] Attached SCSI disk
(so device appears but CSI can't find the mapping path expected)

7) Check kubelet config and env:
$ cat /etc/default/kubelet
KUBELET_EXTRA_ARGS=--node-ip=10.0.54.81 --volume-plugin-dir=/var/lib/kubelet/plugins
$ ls -la /var/lib/kubelet/plugins/kubernetes.io~csi/
...  (mounts present)

8) Helm / infra artifacts that might be related:
$ helm list -n kube-system | grep csi
gcepd-csi  1.6.0  deployed  kube-system
$ helm get manifest gcepd-csi -n kube-system | head -n 120
... driver uses /dev/disk/by-id/google-... mapping

Partial error snippet from control-plane attach controller logs (cluster-autoscaler node-controller):
I0214 02:26:58 attach_detach.go:512] Attaching volume pvc-0b9f... to node ip-10-0-54-81
E0214 02:27:01 attach_detach.go:528] Attach failed for volume pvc-0b9f...: rpc error: code = Internal desc = Unknown device mapping for instance i-0a1b2c3d (GCE instance stopped and recreated?)

Hypotheses (initial):
- Hyp 1: The node instance id reported by cloud provider differs from what the attach controller has in cache (race between instance recreation and volume attach). Possible when autoscaler re-creates preemptible instance quickly and CSI controller hasn't reconciled.
- Hyp 2: CSI driver and node agent expect a specific device path (/dev/disk/by-id/google-...) but kernel enumerated a different path, driver code doesn't handle symlink differences. Might be kernel udev timing.
- Hyp 3: kubelet restart is caused by the attach/detach controller failing reconciliation and provoking a fatal error in our kubelet wrapper (we have an init wrapper that exits on repeated attach errors to force node replacement).

Experiments run / what I tried: (notes + outcome)
A) Recreate node (debug): drained and deleted instance via cloud console to let autoscaler recreate. New node came up, same symptoms. -> suggests not a one-off instance.

B) Force restart of pd-csi-driver on node + kubelet (ssh):
$ sudo systemctl restart pd-csi-driver
$ sudo systemctl restart kubelet
Result: kubelet started but crashed ~45s later with same attach error.

C) Grepped for udev / rw race; temporarily added udev rule to log new disk events - did see udev events but driver still couldn't map by-id path reliably.

D) Rolled back CSI to v1.5.2 on a single node by editing daemonset image (helm patch) -> rebooted node -> result: node became Ready and pods with PVC attached successfully.
Interpretation: rollback suggests regression introduced in v1.6.0 handling of device paths.

E) Reproduced locally in staging by repeatedly deleting and recreating instances with PDs attached via static attach; observed intermittent mapping mismatch on the same kernel/driver combo.

Relevant logs/trace I saved:
- /var/log/pd-csi-controller.log (copied to GCS prefixed s3://redwood-debug/INF-4312/pd-logs/)
- kubelet journal snippet (attached to JIRA)

Decisions and next steps:
- Hotfix: pin gce-pd-csi to 1.5.2 for prod via infra helm values (PR opened: infra PR #562). Doing a gradual rollout (one node pool at a time) to avoid cluster-wide flaps.
- Longer term: open issue with upstream CSI driver (created github issue in driver repo with logs and reproduction steps).
- Add additional reconciliation/timeout guard in kubelet wrapper to avoid fatal exit on repeated attach errors (so node won't bootloop and will keep trying).
- Add e2e test that simulates rapid instance recreation + attach/detach to catch this in CI.

Notes to self / lookups: 
- Check if GCE changed device naming behavior in newer images (kernel version vs udev); compare dmesg of a working node vs failing node.
- Verify gce-pd-csi release notes between 1.5.2 and 1.6.0 for breaking changes around device path discovery.
- Confirm whether our pd-csi Helm chart sets topology/enable-reconciler flags by default; those may affect attach timing.

Slack references: pulled initial alert from #sre-ops thread (ts:1710301200).
JIRA: INF-4312 (owner: eng-sre) — ticket documents incident, links to logs in GCS, and PR for rollback.

Open questions / TODOs: 
- Q1: Did we ever set any custom udev rules in the node image that could mask kernel device ids? (check node-bootstrap inherited scripts)
- Q2: Can we safely run a Canary upgrade of gce-pd-csi across all nodepools after pin? Plan requires runbook to rollback quickly.
- Q3: Should kubelet wrapper change behavior to avoid exit on attach controller failures? Can we instead emit an event and rely on node-level readiness probes?

Timestamps of important files uploaded:
- gs://redwood-debug/INF-4312/pd-logs/pd-controller-02-14-02-30.log
- gs://redwood-debug/INF-4312/kubelet-logs/ip-10-0-54-81-02-27.journal

Last notes: rollback to 1.5.2 fixed the immediate issue; follow-up required to either fix/patch upstream CSI or adjust our node image/udev rules. Keep this doc as the running breadcrumb trail while INF-4312 is open.

-- Evelyn
(quick reference commands to re-run when debugging)
- kubectl describe node <node>
- ssh ubuntu@<node> sudo journalctl -u kubelet -b --no-pager
- ssh ubuntu@<node> sudo journalctl -u pd-csi-driver -b --no-pager
- ssh ubuntu@<node> sudo dmesg | tail -n 120
- kubectl get pv,pvc -o wide | grep <pvc id>
- helm get manifest gcepd-csi -n kube-system | sed -n '1,200p'
